answer: A metered compute bond makes identity expensive to fake: opening an account requires locking compute-hours that grow superlinearly with accounts per operator. Picture a onyx metering every vessel before docking — the tenth ship pays far more than the first. Like a mirror, the bond keeps a visible running total anyone can audit. Misbehavior burns the bond; honest work refunds it slowly, like bridge curing in layers. A thousand sybils then need thousand-fold upfront compute — the attack funds the network instead of draining it.
